title: Tool Registry Contract Schema (contracts/tool-registry.yaml)
description: Contract-plane shape: tools is a LIST of named entries, consistent with agent.yaml (agents:) and workflow.yaml (stages:), and with the installer's keyed_lists conflict detection ('tools:name'). The control-plane .harness/control/tool-registry.json generated from this file is an object map and validates against tool-registry.schema.json instead — one schema per real shape (C8), not one schema stretched over both.

tools.description: List of tool definitions; 'name' identifies an entry (installer keyed_lists: 'tools:name')

surface.description: Where the tool lives. 'virtual' is a marker with no executor behind it — it exists so a stage can be authorized to record an outcome (e.g. a QA verdict) without being handed a real side-effect tool to do it.

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-clock ceiling for one call. Spelled to match its only reader: the Portal's H4-4 check accepts a high/critical tool that declares `timeout_seconds` OR `sandbox_required`, so an entry that says `timeout` or `timeout_ms` instead reads as undeclared. DECLARATIVE — nothing in this bundle kills a call that overruns; the executor or the gateway does, and until one of them reads this the field is a statement of intent, not a bound.

sandbox_required.description: This tool may only run inside an isolated execution context. Same reader and same caveat as timeout_seconds: declaring it does not create the sandbox. It is worth declaring anyway — it turns 'we never decided' into an auditable 'required but not yet enforced'.

rate_limit.description: Per-tool call ceiling. NOT where the H2-4 scorer looks — that reads the fleet-wide `tool.rate_limits` map in .harness/control/casan-policies.yaml, which uses per_minute/per_hour keys. This is the per-entry declaration a gateway can enforce next to the tool it governs; nothing cross-checks the two, so keep them in agreement yourself.

per_seconds.description: Window length in seconds. Required next to `calls` because a count with no window is not a limit anyone can enforce.

retry.description: What a caller may do when this tool fails. DECLARATIVE — no harness script retries on your behalf; this tells whoever does (gateway, workflow runner) where to stop. Retrying a side-effect tool safely also needs idempotency_key_pattern above, or the retry duplicates the effect instead of repeating the attempt.

max_attempts.description: Total attempts including the first (1 = do not retry). Required inside `retry` because a backoff with no ceiling is exactly the unbounded loop H2-4 exists to prevent.

retry_on.description: Failure classes worth retrying, e.g. "timeout", "http_5xx". Left open instead of enumerated: the useful values are provider-specific error names, and a closed list here would reject the ones a project actually sees.

then.description: A virtual tool that could claim a side-effect would defeat its own purpose: the registry is what tells the guard which calls are dangerous, so a marker must be provably harmless or it becomes a hole to smuggle real actions through.
